trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
Titania is a 20th-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 26, +18 to hit with spell attacks). Titania has the following druid spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): druidcraft, poison spray, resistance, thorn whip
	• 1st level (4 slots): charm person, cure wounds, faerie fire, healing word
	• 2nd level (3 slots): heat metal, hold person, moonbeam, spike growth
	• 3rd level (3 slots): call lightning, conjure animals, dispel magic, sleet storm
	• 4th level (3 slots): confusion, dominate beast, grasping vine
	• 5th level (3 slots): awaken, geas, scrying
	• 6th level (2 slots): conjure fey, heal, sunbeam
	• 7th level (2 slots): regenerate, reverse gravity
	• 8th level (1 slots): earthquake, feeblemind
	• 9th level (1 slots): foresight, shapechange

action.name: Crystal Dagger
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d4 + 6) piercing damage plus 22 (4d10) psychic damage. A creature damaged by the dagger must make a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw or be restrained as their skin turns to crystal. The creature may repeat the saving throw at the end of their turn to end the effect. If the creature fails three saving throws, they are turned into a statue of pure crystal and slain. The dagger then magically returns to Titania's hand, provided that it is able to do so.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: Titania can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Titania regains spent legendary actions at the start of her turn.

legendary.name: Crystal Dagger
legendary.text: Titania makes one crystal dagger attack.

legendary.name: Entangle
legendary.text: Titania casts entangle. Treat this like the first level spell of the same name, but Titania does not need to concentrate to maintain its effects.

legendary.name: Plant Stride
legendary.text: Titania may step into a plant or plant based creature within 5 feet of her and teleport to a plant or plant based creature within 300 feet.

fields.spells: Druidcraft, Poison Spray, Resistance, Thorn Whip, Charm Person, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, Healing Word, Heat Metal, Hold Person, Moonbeam, Spike Growth, Call Lightning, Conjure Animals, Dispel Magic, Sleet Storm, Confusion, Dominate Beast, Grasping Vine, Awaken, Geas, Scrying, Conjure Fey, Heal, Sunbeam, Regenerate, Reverse Gravity, Earthquake, Feeblemind, Foresight, Shapechange
fields.description: Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 59 (Indie)

fields.name: Oberon
fields.immune: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If Oberon fails a saving throw she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Lord of Archers
trait.text: Oberon is the best archer in the Multiverse. He does not make ranged weapon attack rolls with disadvantage if he has an opponent within 5 feet. Oberon does make attack rolls with disadvantage when shooting beyond a bow's normal range. Oberon ignores cover when attacking with a bow. Finally, Oberon can roll all damage dice an additional time when determining the extra damage for a critical hit.

trait.name: Invisible
trait.text: Oberon is naturally invisible. This effect cannot be dispelled, though he can suppress it if he so chooses.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Oberon makes four attacks, any of which can be with either his warhammer or shortbow, or uses his Rays of Dawn twice.

action.name: Warhammer
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage or 9 (1d10 + 4) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands, plus 33 (6d10) psychic damage.

action.name: Shortbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d6 + 6) piercing damage, plus 33 (6d10) force damage. If the target is within the normal range and is not behind total cover, Oberon's shot strikes unerringly.

action.name: Rays of Dawn
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d8 + 6) type damage plus 33 (6d10) radiant damage. Creatures damaged by the bow must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. Creatures that fail are blinded and deafened until the end of their next turn.

legendary.name:
Legendary Actions
Oberon Can Take 3 Legendary Actions, Choosing From the Options
Below
legendary.text: Oberon can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Oberon regains spent legendary actions at the start of his turn.

legendary.name: Rays of Dawn
legendary.text: Oberon makes one rays of dawn attack. Through the Forest. Oberon may move up to his speed. This move does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

legendary.name: Mark the Target
legendary.text: Oberon chooses one target he can see. All his attacks against that target inflict an additional 14 (4d6) damage until the end of his next turn.

fields.description: Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 60 (Indie)

fields.name: Queen of Air and Darkness
fields.immune: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks, cold, thunder

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If the Queen of Air and Darkness fails a saving throw she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Invisible
trait.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness is naturally invisible. This effect cannot be dispelled, though she can suppress it if she so chooses.

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. She takes 5 (1d10) force damage if she ends her turn inside an object.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness makes four blighted touch attacks.

action.name: Blighted Touch
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +17 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 31 (4d10 + 9) psychic damage. A creature damaged by this attack must make a DC 24 Constitution saving throw. If they fail they cannot regain hit points until after they complete a long rest.

action.name: Wail of the Damned (recharges 5-6)
action.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness howls. The terrible sound rebounds from walls and seems to be coming from everywhere at once. Every creature within 120 feet of the Queen must make a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 45 (10d8) necrotic damage. A creature that failed the saving throw takes 45 (10d8) necrotic damage at the start of their next turn and must repeat the Wisdom saving throw. This continues until the creature succeeds on its saving throw, ending this effect on itself in a success.

reaction.name: The Void
reaction.text: If a creature within 30 feet of the Queen makes a successful saving throw, the Queen may use her reaction to force them to repeat the save with disadvantage. The creature must use the new save.

legendary.name:
Legendary Actions
Oberon Can Take 3 Legendary Actions, Choosing From the Options
Below
legendary.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Queen of Air and Darkness regains spent legendary actions at the start of her turn.

legendary.name: Shadow Walk
legendary.text: The Queen steps into a shadow and reappears in any shadow within 300 feet.

legendary.name: Swipe
legendary.text: The Queen makes one Blighted Touch attack.

legendary.name: Glimpse of the Eternal
legendary.text: The Queen of Air and Darkness reaches into the mind of a creature within 30 feet and reveals her face. The creature must make a DC 22 Wisdom saving throw or be incapacitated until the end of their next turn.

fields.description: Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 61 (Indie)

name: Ice, Lord of the Dark Hunt

fields.name: Ice, Lord of the Dark Hunt

trait.name: Unearthly Nimbleness
trait.text: Ice suffers no movement reduction from difficult terrain and treats impassable terrain as difficult terrain.

trait.name: Unearthly Hunter
trait.text: Ice scores a critical hit on a roll of a 19 or 20.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Ice's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). Ice can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: hunter's mark
	• 3/day each: jump, longstrider

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Ice makes three attacks, any of which can be with his soul stealing dagger or shortbow.

action.name: Soul Stealing Dagger
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d4 + 4) piercing damage plus 14 (4d6) poison damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by an attack with a soul stealing dagger must make a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. If they fail they are immediately slain, and Ice gains 10 temporary hit points and has advantage on melee attack rolls on his next turn.

action.name: Shortbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d6 + 4) type damage plus 9 (2d8) poison damage.

action.name: Make Them Bleed (special)
action.text: Ice makes a single soul stealing dagger attack against a creature within range. If he hits, the dagger inflicts maximum damage and the creature must make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. If they fail, the creature takes one level of exhaustion. This ability recharges after Ice inflicts a critical hit.

action.name: Sudden Dash (Bonus Action)
action.text: Ice may move up to his full speed. This attack does not provoke opportunity attacks.

fields.spells: Hunter's Mark, Jump, Longstrider
fields.description: Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 62 (Indie)

fields.name: Dragon Throne
fields.languages: can't speak, only communicates with its queen
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Immutable Form
trait.text: The Dragon Throne cannot be polymorphed against its will.

trait.name: Detect Thoughts
trait.text: The Dragon Throne is under a continuous detect thoughts spell. The dragon does not have to concentrate to maintain this spell.

trait.name: Spell Storing
trait.text: The Dragon Throne acts as a ring of spell turning for its occupant

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The Dragon Throne makes one bite and two claw attacks.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d10 + 6) piercing damage plus 18 (4d8) cold damage.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 15 (2d8 + 6) slashing damage.

action.name: Cold Breath (recharge 5-6)
action.text: The Dragon Throne exhales an icy blast in a 50 foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) cold damage on a failed save and half as much on a successful one.

action.name: For the Mistress (Bonus Action)
action.text: If Titania or the Queen of Air and Darkness takes damage within 30 feet of the Dragon Throne, the Throne may use its reaction to absorb the damage. Treat this as if the Throne had been the initial target of the attack. The Throne may use this ability before the queen makes a saving throw.

fields.description:
Do note that although one throne is made of ice and the other of solid shadow and smoke, the statistics for both thrones are the same.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 63 (Indie)

fields.name: Fey Noble

action.name: Rapier
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Shortbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing damage.

action.name: Misty Step (1/Day) (Bonus Action)
action.text: The fey noble casts misty step.

fields.description:
Fey nobles attend both courts. They are the primary players in the convoluted politics of both courts. Mortals find them beautiful, and they find mortals to be useful tools. Nearly every noble belongs to a clan, usually bound by blood. These clans form the basis of fey society and are always beholden to at least one fey lord. Marriages between different clans are supposed to create new alliances, but mostly just cause more chaos.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 64 (Indie)

fields.name: Fey Consort

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Innate Spellcasting. The fey consort's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 14, +6 to hit with spell attacks). The fey consort can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: friends, minor illusion

action.name: Dagger
action.text: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) type damage.

fields.spells: Friends, Minor Illusion
fields.description:
Fey consorts are neither combat veterans or skilled assassins, but they are some of the most dangerous members of either fey court. They are skilled manipulators and spies. They excel at gathering information and spotting corrupt individuals they can manipulate into giving the fey consorts what they want.
	Fey consorts avoid combat whenever possible, leaving that for the more boorish members of the court. Fey consorts are almost perversely fond of mortals, who are easy to manipulate.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 65 (Indie)

fields.name: Dark Hunter

trait.name: Slice the Heel
trait.text: If a dark hunter scores a critical hit, the creature must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have their speed reduced by half for 10 minutes.

action.name: Scimitar
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) slashing damage plus 3 (1d6) poison damage.

action.name: Shortbow
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) piercing damage.

action.name: Howl of the Hunt (Bonus Action)
action.text: As a bonus action, the dark hunter may howl when it sees its prey. Every other dark hunter within 100 feet can hear the howl and may use their reaction to move up to their speed toward the prey.

fields.spells: Friends, Minor Illusion
fields.description:
The Unseelie Court is the home of the dark hunt. The dark hunt is a collection of fey and unique creatures that the Queen of Air and Darkness unleashes on anyone foolish enough to displease her, anger her, or if she's bored. The dark hunt gleefully seeks out its prey. Prizes and honor will be showered on the fey that kills the target of the hunt. Particularly painful or artistic kills will be given even greater honor. Competition amongst the dark hunt is extremely high, and most fey consider the race back to the Unseelie Court to deliver the target's head to be the most exciting part.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 65 (Indie)

fields.name: Baba Yaga
fields.save: Str +19, Dex +12, Con +16, Int +14, Wis +15, Cha +19
fields.resist: acid, cold, fire, lightning, radiant, thunder
fields.immune: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks, necrotic

trait.name: The First Witch
trait.text: Baba Yaga is one of the oldest beings in the multiverse. She was there when magic came into being and has studied its deepest secrets ever since. Baba Yaga knows every spell and can cast them at any time. She must expend spell slots as normal. Baba Yaga may cast any cantrip at will. She has four spell slots apiece for first through third level. She has three spell slots for each level from fourth through sixth. She has two spell slots for each level from seven to nine. Charisma is her usual spellcasting ability (spell save DC 27, +19 to hit with spell attacks) but she does know secrets of magic that allow her to use others. Baba Yaga's spells cannot be countered, but they can be blocked. For example, counterspell and dispel magic automatically fail, but shield and wall of force may still prove effective.

trait.name: Companions
trait.text: For a hermit that lives in a hut that moves from plane to plane, Baba Yaga has many companions. Three knights accompany her, each dressed in elaborate plate mail. The first is adorned in red (her Rising Dawn), the second in white (Midday Sun), and the third in black (Midnight Sky). Each of these knights will come to her aid if summoned, arriving by teleportation the round after she calls. These knights are death knights. In addition to the knights, Baba Yaga is also accompanied by her hound (a hell hound) and her cat (a displacer beast). Twenty skulls line the fence around her hut, and Baba Yaga can call all of the skulls at once. Treat the skulls as flameskulls which appear in any empty space within 300 feet of Baba Yaga the round after she calls. All the creatures appear and act on her initiative and can act immediately after appearing. Baba Yaga can call any or all of the creatures without using an action.

trait.name: Eternally Watching
trait.text: Baba Yaga is aware of any creature within 10 miles of her. She cannot be surprised and always goes first in combat.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
trait.text: If the Baba Yaga fails a saving throw she can choose to automatically succeed.

trait.name: Regeneration
trait.text: Baba Yaga gains 50 hit points at the start of her turn. If a wish spell is used to stop this trait, it doesn't function at the start of Baba Yaga's next turn. Baba Yaga only dies if she starts her turn with 0 hit points and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Baba Yaga makes four iron claw attacks and one bite attack.

action.name: Iron Claws
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 28 (4d8 + 10) slashing damage plus 44 (8d10) necrotic damage. A creature damaged by this attack must make a DC 23 Constitution saving throw. Creatures that fail are knocked prone and stunned until the end of Baba Yaga's next turn.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +19 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 36 (4d12 + 10) piercing damage and the creature must make a DC 23 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 28 (8d6) piercing damage plus 28 (8d6) acid damage as Baba Yaga gnaws on them, and the creature's speed becomes 0 until Baba Yaga releases them. If they fail this saving throw by 5 or more, Baba Yaga's mouth magically grows as the creature magically shrinks, and they are swallowed. Swallowed creatures are deposited in Baba Yaga's stomach and torn apart by stomach acid and the spirits of her previous victims. They are slain and cannot be resurrected until Baba Yaga is slain.

action.name: Cackle (recharge 4-6)
action.text: Baba Yaga throws her head back and cackles madly. Every creature within 120 feet of her must make a DC 24 Wisdom saving throw, taking 110 (20d10) force damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If the creature is vulnerable to a type of damage, then the cackle damage becomes that type of damage in addition to being force damage.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: Baba Yaga can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Baba Yaga regains spent legendary actions at the start of her turn.

legendary.name: Heart of Elements
legendary.text: Baba Yaga chooses one of the following types of energy: acid, cold, fire, lightning, radiant, or thunder. Until she uses this ability again, she is immune to that type of damage.

legendary.name: Iron Claw
legendary.text: Baba Yaga makes two iron claw attacks.

legendary.name: Teleport
legendary.text: Baba Yaga can teleport to any empty space within 300 feet. She may also choose to teleport one of her allies from their current location to an empty space within 300 feet.

fields.description:
The Seelie and Unseelie courts are the political power of the Feywild. But while many of the creatures that live in the plane look to them for leadership, they are not the oldest nor the most powerful beings in the Feywild.
	Baba Yaga is an ancient witch that has been called the mother of hags, the first night hag, the first witch and a thousand other titles besides. She is a wizened figure barely five feet tall, although severely hunched. Her hands are tipped with iron claws, and despite her appearance, she is devastatingly fast. Her eyes are black as coal, and when she smiles it is apparent that her teeth are made of sharpened stones. Baba Yaga smiles a lot.
	Baba Yaga is a mysterious figure within the Feywild. Sometimes helpful, and sometimes a cataclysmic force of nature. She does what she wishes when she wishes and very few creatures have the power to stop her.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 66 (Indie)

fields.name: Hound Archon

trait.name: Angelic Weapons
trait.text: The archon's weapon attacks are magical & deal an extra 2d8 radiant damage on a hit (included in the attack).

trait.name: Bloodscent
trait.text: The archon knows the direction & distance to any creature it has hit with a melee weapon attack in the past hour, if it is on the same plane of existence.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The archon has advantage on saving throws against spells & other magical effects.

trait.name: Planar Sentinel
trait.text: Creatures the archon can see within 60 feet cannot teleport or travel to other planes of existence.

action.name: Greatsword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) slashing damage plus 9 (2d8) radiant damage.

action.name: Change Shape
action.text: The archon magically polymorphs into a canine beast with a challenge rating less than its own, any equipment it carries is absorbed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

fields.description:
These wingless angels have the heads of dogs & the bodies of muscled paladins. They serve as angelic guards & foot soldiers.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 68 (Indie)

fields.name: Jabberwocky

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If the jabberwocky fails a saving throw it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Legendary Insanity
trait.text: The jabberwocky is completely nuts. The endless burbling has taken its toll on the poor creature, leaving a hollow shell of the creature it once was. The jabberwocky is immune to spells from the enchantment school.

trait.name: Limited Flight
trait.text: Calling the jabberwocky a clumsy flier is an immense understatement. Wings, neck, and limbs move in every direction at once and the jabberwocky doesn't fly as much as it falls in a variety of directions. The jabberwocky must start and finish its fly movement on ground. If it doesn't, the jabberwocky falls, taking 1d6 damage for every 10 feet fallen.

trait.name: Vorpal Vulnerability
trait.text: Vorpal swords score a critical hit on the jabberwocky on a roll of a 19 or 20.

trait.name: Burble
trait.text: The jabberwocky constantly talks, whispers, shouts, repeats terrible secrets it could not know, and weeps. The constant noise even affects the minds of those nearby, making communications and spellcasting difficult. Every creature within 120 feet of the jabberwocky is deafened. A spellcaster that attempts to cast a spell within 120 feet of the jabberwocky must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If they fail, the spell is ruined and countered, although the spell slot is still expended. On a success, the spell is cast as normal.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The jabberwocky makes two claw attacks and one burbling bite attack.

action.name: Burbling Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 7) piercing damage plus 11 (2d10) psychic damage. A creature damaged by this attack must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be stunned until the end of the jabberwocky's next turn. If the creature rolls a natural 1 on the saving throw, they are knocked unconscious for 1 minute.

action.name: Claw
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 14 (2d6 + 7) slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +13 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d8 + 7) bludgeoning damage.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The jabberwocky can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The jabberwocky regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Tail
legendary.text: The jabberwocky makes a tail attack.

legendary.name: Indignant Burble (2 Actions)
legendary.text: Something someone does insults the jabberwocky, who lets loose a short indignant shout. Every creature within 50 feet of the jabberwocky must make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) thunder damage on a failed save.

legendary.name: Hop
legendary.text: The jabberwocky flaps its wings and pumps its limbs, taking to the air and landing in an empty space within 40 feet. This random amalgamation of limbs and wings is confusing for attackers and this move does not provoke opportunity attacks.

fields.description:
The jabberwocky is an enigma. It appears near either court seemingly at random, and sages among the fey listen to its constant burbling, trying to ascertain any meaning or portent in the insanity.
	The jabberwocky is a massive dragon shaped creature nearly thirty feet in length. It is a gangly mishmash of limbs, with a head far too large for its neck. Its eyes constantly wander, never looking at anything for very long and its heavy jaws constantly move. The jabberwocky has small wings that are barely able to lift its massive body off the ground.
	Little is known about the history of the jabberwocky. Some sages think it to be a type of dragon, and others a mutilated fiend or celestial. No one really knows. Sages even argue if there is one jabberwocky or if it is a species of dragon native to the Feywild. The only sure thing is that the jabberwocky isn't telling anyone.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 69 (Indie)

fields.name: Lantern Archon
fields.immune: lightning, poison; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

trait.name: Incorporeal Movement
trait.text: The archon can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends it's turn inside an object

trait.name: Variable Illumination
trait.text: The archon sheds bright light in a 5- to 20-foot radius and dim light for the same radius beyond that. It can alter these as a bonus action.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Innate Spellcasting. The archon's spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). The archon can innately cast the following spells, requiring only vocal components:

	• At will: cure wounds, sacred flame

action.name: Smite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) radiant damage and the target becomes visible if it was invisible. Attack rolls against the target are made with advantage until the end of the archon's next turn.

fields.spells: Cure Wounds, Sacred Flame
fields.description:
These wispy entities appear to be harmless balls of floating light to untrained observers. Yet, their ephemeral and benign appearance hides their true natures. They are the departed spirits of great warriors, tasked by the gods with protecting their people.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 70 (Indie)

fields.name: Spell Seeker
fields.languages: understands Infernal but can't speak it

trait.name: Magic Hunter
trait.text: If the Spell Seeker sees a spell cast within 60 feet of it, the Spell Seeker can use its reaction to mark the caster. While marked, the Spell Seeker's Drain Bite attack deals an extra 1d6 necrotic damage to the marked target on a hit. In addition, the spell seeker has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks to track the marked creature. The Spell Seeker can only mark one target at a time.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The spell seeker makes two claw attacks. Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 8 (2d4 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Drain Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. one creature. Hit: 6 (1d6 + 3) necrotic damage and the spell seeker regains hit points equal to half the damage done to the target, rounded down.

reaction.name: Pounce
reaction.text: When the spell seeker can make an attack of opportunity, it can instead use its reaction to attempt to grapple the creature (escape DC 13).

fields.description:
These fiendish creatures resemble hairless pale-white dogs but with elongated legs. Being experts at following magical trails left behind by arcane uses, they are frequently used by both bounty hunters to track down unlawful mages and by Devils who are looking for someone to enslave. Once one of these creatures mark a target, they will stop at almost nothing until they catch their quarry.

Source:	Tasha's Scrapped Book p. 70 (Indie)

fields.description:
Azân is a fiend who opened up a shop after being cast out from Hell. His many magical treasures have been collected over centuries of travel to everywhere from the biggest trading hubs in the largest cities to the most obscure places at the edge of the world — and across many different planes of existence. Azân's shop can be found anywhere — or nowhere at all, depending on who is looking.

Only a handful of creatures know that Azân used to be a respected fiendish lord, who led and lost a rebellion against an archfiend on his native plane. As a result, Azân had his horns and titles stripped away and was banished from his homeland.
	What started as an eternal and purposeless existence, wandering from city to city across planes and continents, eventually became Azân's new purpose. Equipped only with his keen mind, a deep appreciation of the arcane, and a warm demeanor, Azân began picking up exotic trinkets, rare materials, and other oddities on his long journeys.
	Though Azân no longer has the fighting spirit of his youth, his infernal magic and ageless body are as strong as ever. Azân is confident in the knowledge that most mortal beings are no immediate danger to him, which has made him rather lax over the years.

Roleplaying Azân and Jaziel:
Having lived for nearly a millennium, it takes a lot to rattle Azân, who always seems to have a warm and welcoming attitude. He laughs wholeheartedly at jokes, even those aimed at himself, and meets even direct threats with a shrug and a chuckle. While Azân won't share the details of his past ("I sell goods, not stories, friend, and what I have to tell ain't worth much to you anyway") he is a polite listener with a soft spot for outcasts and underdogs.
	In stark contrast to Azân's friendly demeanor, his companion Jaziel carefully scrutinizes every action customers take. While he resembles a dog – albeit with a long and slender tail – Jaziel is in truth a gydrash, a highly intelligent celestial creature. Jaziel likes to hide the fact that he can speak, but if someone touches the rare merchandise without permission, he breaks his silence to warn them that "I would think twice before doing that" in a cold, nasal voice. If a character tries to pat Jaziel, he growls fiercely, prompting Azân to laughingly explain that "Jaziel doesn't like to be touched. Best take your hands off before he does."
	Despite his gruff exterior, Jaziel loves a good trade – if the characters are serious about doing business, he will quickly warm to them.

Bargaining:
Already very wealthy and having few vices, gold holds no real value to Azân. As a result, he usually initiates bargains by naming a price that's a little too good, before a quick telepathic objection from Jaziel makes him correct himself: "That'll be 400 gold. Oh, wait you know what, better say 500 gold pieces!"
	Likewise, haggling with Azân isn't too difficult and he may even be persuaded to drop his prices all the way down to half the item's value. This, however, causes Jaziel to "break cover" and speak up: "Stop it, you fool, you're practically giving it away!" When this happens, Azân usually defers to his companion and brings the price back up.

Biases:
Azân always roots for the underdog. Whether that's the tiefling outcast, the disheveled urchin, or the fighter who's lost an arm, Azân offers discounts to characters who are down on their luck or have the odds against them (ignoring Jaziel's objections).
	On the other hand, Azân has a clear disdain for those who believe themselves above others, such as arrogant nobles or self-centered bards. Customers who behave haughtily or are overly flashy irk the otherwise good-natured merchant and will find his prices to be higher than usual.

Shop Security:
Azân's shop is kept safe by the fiend himself and the watchful eyes of Jaziel, and his wares can be quickly stowed away in a portable hole.

Powerful Fiend:
Despite his relaxed attitude, Azân is more than capable of defending himself. He is protected not only by his magical items but also by his fiendish magic. If Azân is ever in a situation too hot to handle, he will grab the makeshift door he carries in his portable hole and use his key to anywhere to magically teleport away.

Guardian Angel:
Jaziel's truesight gives any character who attempts to steal from the shop a hard time. If a character is caught attempting to pocket something, Jaziel telepathically alerts Azân. As long as the characters don't respond with violence, Azân tries to deescalate the situation by shrugging the attempted theft off as a misunderstanding.

Never Unattended:
Azân's stand and most of his merchandise are placed near a magical black cloth, which works as a portable hole. This means that Azân can pack down his entire shop in a matter of seconds – which he does whenever he goes anywhere, never leaving the shop unattended.

Source:	Wanderer's Guide To Merchants & Magic p. 12 (Indie)

fields.description:
Brumir Bronzeforge, stout dwarf and accomplished merchant, has been spearheading the Bronzeforge Clan's most lucrative business dealings for almost a century. In the Bronzeforge Halls, Brumir converts his clan's marvelous creations into vast amounts of gold and gemstones – with an emphasis on the latter.
	The Bronzeforge Halls can be placed in any city where dwarves live and prosper. The halls would fit especially well in the merchant's district of a larger city where fortunes can be made satisfying a demand for well-crafted – and even magic – trinkets, weapons, and suits of armor.

Brumir is a short and plump middle-aged dwarf who displays an impressive gray-brown beard and has a passion for dwarven ale and gemstones – a dwarf's dwarf, in other words.
	Brumir was in no way fated to run the most profitable unit in the Bronzeforge Clan's business empire. As a youth, he showed no talent as an craftsman at the family's anvils, nor prominence on the battlefield, or interest in religious teachings. Short on options, Brumir's father decided that his youngest son was to be trained as a merchant.
	As luck had it, Brumir was a natural-born salesman. Bartering and haggling came easy to the young dwarf, and the pursuit of wealth – especially deliciously large gemstones, which Brumir has a particular weakness for – drove Brumir more than anything ever had. For nearly a century, Brumir has worked hard to make the Bronzeforge Halls into a well-known, well-protected, and successful emporium of high-quality armor, weapons, and jewelry.

Roleplaying Brumir:
As long as Brumir smells profits, he can be a gracious and downright pleasant host, who will take the time to sit down and trade pleasantries with customers.
	Brumir has a strong sense of honor and is always true to his word. He abhors lying (though mild exaggeration has never hurt anyone!) and confronts liars with tirades such as: "Ha! Sure 'bout that, laddie?
Smells like a bunch of good ol' bauxite refinery!"
	Brumir has long since learned to cope with insults aimed at him and handles even dire threats with a defusing smile. The stocky dwarf, however, has a hard time accepting insults aimed at the Bronzeforge Clan or the craftsmanship of the items in his inventory. If a customer crosses this line, Brumir's face darkens and his voice grows cold: "'Ware yer words now, friend. Ye're in the Bronzeforge Halls and we ain't no band of bumblin' bugbears to be pushed around as ye like!"

Bargaining:
Brumir is a skilled merchant who drives an extremely hard bargain. If he is selling, which is his preference, he starts out asking for well above an item's true value.
	Stubborn himself, Brumir respects persistence in his customers. If faced with a tough bargainer, he may lower his prices to about the item's market value, but fights back against further discounts: "Thinkin' me softer than sandstone, lass? By me ma's beard, what ye suggest is daylight robbery!"
	One thing that can land a favorable deal in Brumir's shop is large gemstones. Brumir has such an extreme love for valuable gems, the larger the better, that it borders on the obsessive. Brumir's avarice may cause him to pay up to twice the market value for gemstones worth more than 1,000 gp.

Biases:
Brumir respects elven craftsmanship, but he holds no love for the elves themselves, as he regards them as arrogant and annoying know-it-alls. Elves are likely to find Brumir's prices even steeper than usual.
	Conversely, Brumir usually offers discounts to any dwarf who shares his ideals and humor. Dwarf or not, Brumir also respects anyone who has a proper beard – even elves, although he's "never met an elf with a beard, and that's how I be knowin' them pointy-eared bastards ain't to be trusted!"

Shop Security:
Brumir is by no means a warrior (he has the statistics of a noble). Aware of this fact, the dwarf merchant has taken numerous steps to protect himself and, most importantly, his clan's inventory.

Stripped of Weapons:
Brumir's cousin, a priest named Tribur Bronzeforge, acts as gatekeeper to the Bronzeforge Halls and asks each character to hand over their weapons to a steward upon entry to the shop. Additionally, he casts a zone of truth and asks all characters who wish to enter if they intend to harm anyone or steal any items while inside the shop. Anyone who can't answer a clear no to that question is refused entry.

Antimagic Field:
The bronze murals in the Bronzeforge Halls are not just for display. The murals create an antimagic field spell that suppresses the effects of any magic items and renders it impossible to cast any spells while inside the shop. The effect can only be ended by destroying at least six 5-foot sections of the murals (AC 16; 30 hit points; damage threshold 15; resistance to all nonmagical damage, and immunity to piercing, poison, and psychic damage).

Elite Guardians:
As a more tangible protective measure, a squad of bronzeforge elite guards stands ready to protect the Bronzeforge Clan's inventory. Day or night, at least two guards stand watch outside the Bronzeforge Halls and at least four guards remain close to Brumir and the valuable inventory.

Adamantine Vault:
Most of the shop's magic items and precious metals are locked inside an adamantine vault when the shop is closed at night. The vault is hidden behind one of the bronze murals and can be found with a successful DC 25 Intelligence (Investigation) check. Once the mural, which is set on hinges, is pushed aside, a 5-foot-square adamantine door is visible. The door is locked and can only be opened with a key that Brumir keeps on a chain around his neck.

Source:	Wanderer's Guide To Merchants & Magic p. 17 (Indie)

trait.text: Elpha wears a cat's eye amulet, a cloak of protection, and a ring of alarm.

trait.text:
Elpha can add her Intelligence modifier (+4) to one damage roll of any evocation spell
she casts.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance

These creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell. If a successful save means a chosen creature would take half damage from the spell, it instead takes no damage from it.

Elpha casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using
Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 16):

fields.languages: Understands Common, Draconic, Elvish, and Sylvan, but doesn't speak

trait.name: Pounce
trait.text: If Calypso moves at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a claw attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

trait.name: Spellmane Necklace
trait.text: If Calypso would be reduced to 0 hit points, her current hit point total instead becomes 125 and she transforms into a spellmane lion for 1 minute. As a spellmane lion, Calypso has a Strength and Constitution score of 18 and an AC of 16. Calypso can also trigger this transformation as a bonus action.

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Devour Magic (Spellmane Lion Form Only)

On a failure, the creature loses the highest level spell slot it has available of 5th level or lower and takes psychic damage equal to 1d10 + the level of the spell slot. Calypso gains temporary hit points equal to the combined level of spell slots consumed this way.

fields.name: Clockwork Worm
fields.resist: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Clockwork Creature
trait.text:
If the worm takes 60 damage or more on a single turn (or half as much from a creature
inside it), the worm's mechanical body malfunctions. The first time this happens, the worm's sensors malfunction and it loses its blindsight. The second time it happens, the worm's speed is halved and it can no longer take the Multiattack action.

trait.name: Critical Malfunction
trait.text: When the worm is reduced to 0 hit points, it explodes. Each creature within 30 feet must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage and 28 (8d6) piercing damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

trait.name: Tunneler
trait.text: The worm can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 10-foot diameter tunnel in its wake.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The worm attacks with its Bite and Propulsion Tail.

action.name: Bite
action.text:
Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 22 (3d8 + 9) piercing damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature, it must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw or be swallowed by the worm. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the worm, and it takes 21 (6d6) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the worm's turns.
A swallowed creature can make a DC 15 Dexterity check as an action to try to squeeze itself out through the gaps in the worm's metallic armor. On a success, the creature emerges from worm's body to land prone in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it.

action.name: Propulsion Tail
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (3d6 + 9) bludgeoning damage, and the target must make a DC 22 Strength saving throw if it is Large or smaller. On a failure, the target is hurled up to 60 feet horizontally in a direction of the worm's choice and lands prone, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it was thrown.

fields.description: Source:	Wanderer's Guide To Merchants & Magic p. 25 (Indie)

fields.skill: Athletics +11, Insight +9, Perception +9, Sleight of Hand +7

trait.name: Charge
trait.text: If Hestannia moves at least 10 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a Gore attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 19 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away and knocked prone.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance
trait.text: When Hestannia fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Reckless
trait.text: At the start of Hestannia's turn, she can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls she makes during that turn, but attack rolls against her have advantage until the start of her next turn.

trait.name: Tattoo of Devastation (1 Use)
trait.text: Before she makes an attack, Hestannia can choose to make the attack roll with advantage and the tattoo disappears. If she does, and the attack hits, it is a critical hit.

trait.name: Tattoo of Freedom (1 Use)
trait.text: When spells and other magical effects would reduce Hestannia's speed to 0 hit points or cause her to be paralyzed or restrained, this effect is negated against her, and the tattoo disappears. She can also speak the tattoo's command word as a bonus action to automatically escape from nonmagical restrains, such as manacles or a creature that has her grappled. Once she does so, the tattoo disappears.

trait.name: Tattoo of Spell Turning (1 Use)
trait.text:
When Hestannia is the target of a spell or spell attack that targets only her, she can choose to make her saving throw against that spell with advantage, or that the spell attack has disadvantage against her, and the tattoo disappears. If she successfully saves against the spell or the spell attack misses her, the spell has no effect on her and
instead targets the caster, using the slot level, spell save DC, attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the caster. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts until the end
of the caster's next turn, even if they choose not to maintain their concentration on it.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
trait.text: While Hestannia is not wearing any armor, her Armor Class equals 10 + her Dexterity modifier + her Constitution modifier.

Magnus casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):

	• 3/day each: animal friendship, cure wounds, fog cloud, longstrider
	• 1/day each: lesser restoration, pass without trace, spike growth

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (2/Turn)
legendary.text: Magnus can take 2 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Magnus regains spent legendary actions at the start of his turn.

legendary.name: Attack
legendary.text: Magnus makes a weapon attack.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Magnus casts a spell.

fields.name: Ezkellion

trait.name: Special Equipment
trait.text: Ezkellion carries a chronomancer's staff.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance
trait.text: If Ezkellion fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Chronomancer's Staff
trait.text: Ezkellion can't be surprised and has advantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. Additionally, other creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against him.

action.name: Temporary Stasis
action.text:
A creature within 60 feet that Ezkellion can see must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution
saving throw or be incapacitated and have a speed of 0 until the end of Ezkellion's next turn or until it takes damage.

action.name: Time Scramble
action.text:
A creature within 60 feet that Ezkellion can see must succeed on a DC 21 Constitution
saving throw or be incapacitated and have a speed of 0 until the end of Ezkellion's next turn or until it takes damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
Ezkellion casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using
Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 21):

	• At will: dispel magic, mage armor 
	• 3/day each: delayed blast fireball, dominate monster, forcecage, globe of invulnerability, mind blank
	• 1/day each: imprisonment, power word kill, time stop

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: Ezkellion can take 3 legendary actions. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. Ezkellion regains spent legendary actions at the start of his turn.

legendary.name: Revert Time
legendary.text: After a creature's turn, Ezkellion reverts time for himself to just before that creature's turn started. He magically appears in the spot he was in when the creature's turn started, regains any hit points he lost during the creature's turn, and any conditions or effects that began on him since the start of that creature's turn no longer affect him.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Ezkellion casts a spell.

fields.name: Vil
fields.resist: damage from spells; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Special Equipment

trait.name: Ioun Stone of Mastery
trait.text: Vil's proficiency bonus is increased by 1 (included in their stat block).

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Vil uses Robe of Stars and casts a spell.

action.name: Astral Jaunt
action.text: Vil uses their robe of stars to enter the Astral Plane along with everything they are wearing or  carrying. They remain there until they use an action to return to the plane they were on, appearing in the last space they occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.

action.name: Robe of Stars
action.text: Vil tears off a star from their robe of stars to create seven glowing darts of magical force. Each dart hits a creature within 120 feet of Vil, dealing 3 (1d4 + 1) force damage.

action.name: Spellcasting
action.text:
Vil casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using

	• At will: chill touch (as a 17th-level spellcaster), mage hand, minor illusion
	• 3/day each: detect thoughts, dispel magic, mage armor*, polymorph
	• 1/day each: chain lightning, mass suggestion, mind blank, plane shift, stoneskin*, teleport, time stop

*Vil casts these spells on themselves before combat.

action.name: Shapeshift
action.text: Vil polymorphs into a Small or Medium humanoid they have seen, or back into their true form. Their statistics, other than their size, are the same in each form. Any equipment they are wearing or carrying isn't transformed. Vil reverts to their true form if they die.

fields.skill: Acrobatics +7, Arcana +5, Deception +7, Insight +7, Perception +7, Persuasion +7, Stealth +7

trait.name: Special Equipment
trait.text: Xin wears a ring of invisibility and carries a katana of the deathtouched.

trait.name: Death Ward
trait.text: When Xin is reduced to 0 hit points, he instead drops to 1 hit point.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance
trait.text: If Xin fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
trait.text: While Xin is wearing no armor and wielding no shield, his AC includes his Wisdom modifier.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Xin makes two weapon attacks.

action.name: Katana of the Deathtouched +1

action.name: Ring of Invisibility
action.text:
Xin turns invisible. He remains invisible until he attacks or casts a spell, or uses a bonus
action to become visible.

action.name: Command (Bonus Action)
action.text: A friendly creature within 30 feet of Xin can make a weapon attack as a reaction.

reaction.name: Deathtouched
reaction.text: When Xin reduces a creature to 0 hit points, he gains 12 temporary hit points.

reaction.name: Parry
reaction.text: Xin adds 5 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him made by an attacker he can see.

fields.description: Source:	Wanderer's Guide To Merchants & Magic p. 86 (Indie)

fields.name: Elite Warrior Monk

trait.name: Ki Penetration
trait.text: The monk ignores all bonuses to AC granted by spells and equipment.

trait.name: Unarmored Defense
trait.text: While the monk is wearing no armor and wielding no shield, its AC includes its Wisdom modifier.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The monk makes two attacks.

action.name: Force Strike
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) force damage, and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

action.name: Stunning Strike
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) force damage and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of the monk's next turn.

fields.name: Cerebrax
fields.resist: poison, psychic; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: The cerebrax has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Mind Armor
trait.text: The cerebrax has a psionic field around itself that gives it an AC of 16.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting (Psionics)
trait.text:
The cerebrax's innate spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 15, +7 to hit with spell attacks). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no components:

	• At will: detect thoughts, levitate, minor illusion
	• 3/day: hypnotic pattern, misty step
	• 1/day: see invisibility, shield

action.name: Tentacle
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d8 + 3) slashing damage.

action.name: Mind Blast (Recharge 2-3)
action.text: The cerebrax magically emits psychic energy in a 90-foot cone. Each creature in that area must succeed on a DC 16 Intelligence saving throw or take 13 (2d8 + 4) psychic damage. If the creature(s) are spellcasters and fail the save, the cerebrax also drains three spell slots below 4th level. It gains 10 temporary hit points each time it drains spell slots from a creature.

fields.spells: detect thoughts, levitate, minor illusion, hypnotic pattern, misty step, see invisibility, shield
fields.description:
The first monsters that entered the world through Riftgates were the cerebrax. They are from another world ruled entirely by psionic creatures. Oswald's disruption of the fabric of time and space was quickly noticed by these creatures. They brought a strange curse with them and began to search for magic.

	Magic Hunters. These aberrations hunt spellcasters and drain their powers. This process fuels the psionic monsters. Having searched the multiverse for magical power they were very pleased to have found Oswald's world.

	Mind Control. Cerebrax are insane, foul beings. They want to eventually take over the entire multiverse. The aberrations know they can't compete with powerful spellcasters like Oswald, so lesser magic-users are their usual targets.

	Neural Network. Cerebrax can communicate with others of their kind, even through portals like Riftgates. They share a hive mind where they can access each others' memories.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 7 (Indie)

fields.name: Great Eight, Oswald Myrr

trait.name: Master Transmuter
trait.text:
Oswald can use an action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored within his transmuter's stone in a single burst. When he does so, he can choose on of the following effects. His transmuter's stone is destroyed and can't be remade until he finishes a long rest.

	Major Transformation. He can transmute one nonmagical object-no larger than a 5-foot cube-into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lesser value. He must spend 10 minutes handling the object to transform it.

	Panacea. He removes all curses, diseases, and poisons affecting a creature that he touches with the transmuter's stone. The creature also regains all its hit points.

	Restore Life. He casts the raise dead spell on a creature he touches with the transmuter's stone, without expending a spell slot or needing to have the spell in his spell book.

	Restore Youth. He touches the transmuter's stone to a willing creature, and that creature's apparent age is reduced by 3d10 years, to a minimum of 13 years. This effect doesn't extend the creature's lifespan.

trait.name: Minor Alchemy
trait.text: He can temporarily alter the physical properties of one nonmagical object, changing it from one substance to another. He performs a special alchemical procedure on one object composed entirely of wood, stone (but not a gemstone), iron, copper, or silver, transforming it into a different one of those materials. For each 10 minutes he spends performing the procedure, he can transform up to 1 cubic foot of material. After 1 hour, or until he loses his concentration, the material reverts to its original substance.

trait.name: Shapechanger
trait.text: He can cast the polymorph spell without expending a spell slot. When he does so, he can only target himself and transform into a beast whose challenge rating is 1 or lower. Once he casts polymorph in this way, he can't do so again until he finishes a short or long rest.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
Oswald is a 20th-level wizard. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, message, prestidigitation
	• 1st level (4 slots): expeditious retreat, feather fall, longstrider, magic missile, shield
	• 2nd level (3 slots): alter self, darkvision, invisibility, misty step, scorching ray, spider climb
	• 3rd level (3 slots): counterspell, fireball, gaseous form, haste, meld into stone, water breathing
	• 4th level (3 slots): fabricate, polymorph, stone shape
	• 5th level (3 slots): animate objects, control wind, modify memory, passwall, raise dead
	• 6th level (2 slots): flesh to stone, wind walk
	• 7th level (2 slots): etherealness, reverse gravity
	• 8th level (1 slot): control weather, mind blank
	• 9th level (1 slot): gate

action.name: Staff of Myrr
action.text: Melee Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d12 + 1) bludgeoning damage plus 22 (5d8) force damage.

fields.spells: fire bolt, light, mage hand, message, prestidigitation, expeditious retreat, feather fall, longstrider, magic missile, shield, alter self, darkvision, invisibility, misty step, scorching ray, spider climb, counterspell, fireball, gaseous form, haste, meld into stone, water breathing, fabricate, polymorph, stone shape, animate objects, control wind, modify memory, passwall, raise dead, flesh to stone, wind walk, etherealness, reverse gravity, control weather, mind blank, gate
fields.description:
Oswald Myrr is a legendary wizard and a new member of the Alliance of the Griffon. Some call him the Wizard of Zogg, after his homeland. Oswald currently lives in a secret woodland manor on the continent of Naern. The people of Zogg and Myrr believe the wizard died 500 years ago. However, he is still alive and on a path of redemption. Long ago he was banished from the Wizard Council for his hazardous experiments. After causing so much turmoil, the ancient mage has joined the Alliance to try to make things right. He usually rides a pegasus as his mount.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 147 (Indie)

fields.name: Mary Myrr, Night Hag
fields.resist: cold, fire; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks not made with silvered weapons

trait.name: Magic Resistance
trait.text: Mary has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Mary's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 16, +8 to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: chill touch, detect magic, magic missile, minor illusion
	• 2/day each: hypnotic pattern, misty step, plane shift (self only), ray of enfeeblement, scorching ray (3rd level), sleep, vampiric touch (4th level)
	• 1/day each: banishment, darkness, dispel magic, fog cloud, modify memory

action.name: Claws (Hag Form Only)
action.text: Melee Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) slashing damage plus 22 (5d8) necrotic damage.

action.name: Change Shape
action.text: Mary magically polymorphs into a Small or Medium female humanoid, or back into her true form. Her statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying is transformed. She reverts to her true form if she dies.

action.name: Etherealness
action.text: Mary magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. To do so, she must have a heartstone in her possession.

action.name: Nightmare Haunting (1/Day)
action.text: While on the Ethereal Plane, Mary magically touches a sleeping humanoid on the Material Plane. A protection from evil and good spell cast on the target prevents this contact, as does a magic circle. As long as the contact persists, the target has dreadful visions. If these visions last for at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from its rest, and its hit point maximum is reduced by 5 (1d10). If this effect reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and if the target was evil, its soul is trapped in the hag's soul bag. The reduction to the target's hit point maximum lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

fields.spells: chill touch, detect magic, magic missile, minor illusion, hypnotic pattern, misty step, plane shift, ray of enfeeblement, scorching ray, sleep, vampiric touch, banishment, darkness, dispel magic, fog cloud, modify memory
fields.description:
Oswald's mother is a horrid, insane night hag. She fell in love with Edmund Myrr and was heartbroken when their marriage ended.

	Mad Hag. When Mary lost her mind, she began to wander into other worlds. On her journey she headed further and further down a dark path.

	Smother Mother. She could never leave her son alone as he grew. Mary became obsessed with the talented Oswald. This behavior drove her gifted son to leave and never return.

	Lost Love. At the core of her madness is a broken heart. Her husband didn't just leave her, he didn't love her anymore. While Edmund quickly forgot about his wife, she could never get over him.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 148 (Indie)

fields.name: Edmund Myrr, Lich King
fields.languages: Common, Abyssal, Draconic, Elvish, Giant, Infernal
fields.immune: poison; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If Edmund fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Rejuvenation
trait.text: If he has his phylactery, he gains a new body in 1d6 days, regaining all of his hit points and becoming alive again. The new body appears within 120 feet of the phylactery.

trait.name: Turn Resistance
trait.text: Edmund has advantage on saving throws against any effect that turns undead.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
Edmund is a 20th-level wizard. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 23, +15 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): chill touch, fire bolt, mage hand, prestidigitation, ray of frost
	• 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, magic missile, shield, thunderwave
	• 2nd level (3 slots): detect thoughts, invisibility, mirror image
	• 3rd level (3 slots): animate dead, counterspell, dispel magic, fireball
	• 4th level (3 slots): blight, dimension door, ice storm
	• 5th level (3 slots): cloudkill, contagion, scrying
	• 6th level (2 slots): create undead, disintegrate, globe of invulnerability
	• 7th level (2 slots): finger of death, plane shift
	• 8th level (1 slot): dominate monster, power word stun
	• 9th level (1 slot): power word kill

action.name: Void Staff
action.text: Melee Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (3d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage plus 22 (5d8) necrotic damage.

legendary.name: Cantrip
legendary.text: He casts a cantrip.

legendary.name: Frightening Gaze (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Edmund fixes his gaze on one creature he can see within 10 feet of him. The target must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw against this magic or become frightened for 1 minute. The frightened target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a target's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to Edmund's gaze for the next 24 hours.

legendary.name: Disrupt Life (Costs 3 Actions)
legendary.text: Each non-undead creature within 30 feet of Edmund must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw against this magic, taking 35 (10d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

fields.spells: chill touch, fire bolt, mage hand, prestidigitation, ray of frost, detect magic, magic missile, shield, thunderwave, detect thoughts, invisibility, mirror image, animate dead, counterspell, dispel magic, fireball, blight, dimension door, ice storm, cloudkill, contagion, scrying, create undead, disintegrate, globe of invulnerability, finger of death, plane shift, dominate monster, power word stun, power word kill
fields.description:
Edmund Myrr is Oswald's father, a broken and disillusioned wizard who turned to the dark side and became a lich.

	Dark Path. Fed up with the restrictions of the Wizard Council, Edmund took drastic action. He met with necromancers from the Void and threw himself off Grim Rock. Then the evil spellcasters helped him return to the world as a Lich King. Over a short period of time, Edmund took his place as one of the seven undead Kings of the Void.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 149 (Indie)

fields.name: The Waugan
fields.immune: cold, fire, lightning, poison; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
fields.conditionImmune: charmed, deafened, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
trait.text: If the Waugan fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magical Weapons
trait.text: The Waugan's weapon attacks are magical.

trait.name: Siege Monster
trait.text: The Waugan does double damage to objects and structures.

trait.name: Undertow
trait.text: As a bonus action when the Waugan is underwater, it can cause all water within 90 feet of it to be difficult terrain for other creatures until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Water Breathing
trait.text: The Waugan can breathe only underwater.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The Waugan makes one bite attack and two fist attacks.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +18 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 32 (5d8 + 10) piercing damage.

action.name: Fist
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (3d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wave Attack (Recharge 5-6)
action.text: The Waugan creates waves and sends them out in a 90-foot cone. Any creatures in the area must make a DC 21 Constitution saving throw or take 42 (12d6) bludgeoning damage, half as much damage on a save.

reaction.name: Swat Away
reaction.text: In response to being hit by a ranged weapon attack, the Waugan can swat the projectile away with its tail and take no damage.

legendary.name: Legendary Actions (3/Turn)
legendary.text: The Waugan can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The Waugan regains spent legendary actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
legendary.text: Detect. The Waugan makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

legendary.name: Ink Jet
legendary.text: The Waugan shoots out of jet of ink from its mouth in a 120 ft. line, 5 feet wide. Any creatures in range must make a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw or take 35 (10d6) bludgeoning damage. In addition, the target is blinded until the end of its next turn.

legendary.name: Tail Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
legendary.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +18 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. Hit: 23 (3d8 + 10) bludgeoning damage.

fields.description:
The only creature larger than krakens is the Waugan. This immense titan travels around the entire ocean. At times it can also be found swimming through huge sea caves. It is a solitary creature and has no allies except for an aquarian wizard named Kairos (page 12).

There's Always a Bigger Fish. This massive monster hunts constantly and needs a great deal of nourishment. It feeds on whales, killer whales, dolphins, seals, sea lions, and pretty much anything it wants.

	Sizeable Impact. The Waugan is so powerful it can devastate an undersea castle or settlement in minutes. Some people say that it does more damage than an earthquake or tsunami. Entire sahuagin and merfolk colonies have been destroyed by this titan.

	Secluded Sea Cave. Legends say that the Waugan inhabits a mammoth sea cave. The creature has looted many of the ships it has sunk and taken the bounty. Therefore, most scholars believe a sizeable treasure hoard must be stowed in its cave.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 10 (Indie)

fields.name: Great Eight, Kairos

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: Kairos can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Empowered Evocation
trait.text: Kairos adds +7 to the damage rolls of any wizard evocation spell he casts.

trait.name: Potent Cantrip
trait.text: His damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against his cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

trait.name: Sculpt Spells
trait.text: Kairos can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of his evocation spells. When he casts an evocation spell that affects other creatures that he can see, he can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

trait.name: Slippery
trait.text: Kairos has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple.

trait.name: Spellcasting
trait.text:
Kairos is a 10th-level wizard. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 19, +11 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:

	• Cantrips (at will): fire bolt, light, mage hand, message, prestidigitation
	• 1st level (4 slots): detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, shield
	• 2nd level (3 slots): darkvision, detect thoughts, scorching ray, see invisibility
	• 3rd level (3 slots): dispel magic, lightning bolt, water breathing
	• 4th level (3 slots): control water, dimension door, greater invisibility
	• 5th level (2 slots): cone of cold, conjure elemental

action.name: Quarterstaff
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) bludgeoning damage.

fields.spells: fire bolt, light, mage hand, message, prestidigitation, detect magic, mage armor, magic missile, shield, darkvision, detect thoughts, scorching ray, see invisibility, dispel magic, lightning bolt, water breathing, control water, dimension door, greater invisibility, cone of cold, conjure elemental
fields.description:
Kairos is a member of the Wizard Council who exiled Oswald Myrr. He is also a master of the School of Evocation. This aquarian has big ambitions and is constantly scheming from his lair in a sunken ship. A rival of King Nemos (page 22), he is well-connected in the merfolk community.

	Thought Bubble. This highly intelligent aquarian can be his own worst enemy. His mind never seems to rest and he has got lost in his thoughts on more than a few occasions.

	Scheming Seaman. Kairos is seeking to overthrow King Nemos with the help of sahuagin and aquarian rebels. He uses a unique conch shell to summon the Waugan.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 12 (Indie)

fields.name: Aquarian

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: The aquarian can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Slippery
trait.text: The aquarian has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Atlantia's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 15, +7 to spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: blade ward, message, minor illusion
	• 3/day each: comprehend languages, darkness, detect magic
	• 1/day each: blur, dimension door, suggestion

action.name: Swordfish Sword
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. one target. Hit: 7 (1d10 + 2) slashing damage.

action.name: Net
action.text: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 5/15 ft. one Large or smaller creature. Hit: The target is restrained. A creature can use its action to make a DC 11 Strength check to free itself or another creature in a net, ending the effect on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 11) frees the target without harming it and destroys the net.

fields.description:
Living under the sea are several unique races, and one of the least known are the aquarians. Some folks have heard about a famous gangster known as the Codfather. Most don't realize that he is an aquarian. This race of secretive fish people lives far from most other humanoid communities.

	Fish Folk. The aquarians are ruled by a nasty queen named Atlantia (page 14). A few of these creatures live on land, the infamous Codfather being the most well-known of them.

	Undersea City. At the center of the aquarian society is Nautilus, their capital city. It is composed of extensive sea caves and labyrinthian tunnels. Other sea creatures, including many schools of fish, seals, sharks, and octopi share the settlement.

	Uneasy Alliance. The sahuagin used to be enemies of the aquarians but a recent treaty has changed all that. However, having an alliance with the devious sea devils is never easy. A missing aquarian scouting party has raised fears that the sahuagin cannot be trusted.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 13 (Indie)

fields.name: Atlantia the Aquarian Queen

trait.name: Amphibious
trait.text: Atlantia can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Slippery
trait.text: Atlantia has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape a grapple.

trait.name: Innate Spellcasting
trait.text:
Atlantia's innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 15, +7 to spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

	• At will: blade ward, message, minor illusion
	• 3/day each: comprehend languages, darkness, detect magic
	• 1/day each: blur, dimension door, suggestion

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: Atlantia makes four tentacle attacks.

action.name: Tentacles
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (1d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Ink Cloud (Recharges after a Short Rest)
action.text: A 60-foot-radius cloud of ink extends all around Atlantia if she is underwater. The area is heavily obscured for 1 minute, although a significant current can disperse the ink. After releasing the ink, Atlantia can use the Dash action as a bonus action.

fields.spells: blade ward, message, minor illusion, comprehend languages, darkness, detect magic, blur, dimension door, suggestion
fields.description:
The cold, heartless leader of the aquarians is Atlantia. She rules with an iron fist and crushes any opposition by force. Her four tentacles are always busy grabbing objects and touching her surroundings. Coral statues of her likeness are found throughout Nautilus, the aquarians' biggest settlement.

	Fish Queen. The queen lives in a massive sea cave at the center of Nautilus. As she is one of the largest aquarians, her home is very spacious. She loves shiny, precious objects and hides them away in a large treasure vault.

	Two Schools of Thought. A number of aquarians have left the sea to live on land amongst humans and other humanoids. However, the queen and most of the aquarian leadership are set against this. They want aquarians to live in the sea and remain part of their community.

	Elite Entourage. A group of elite aquarian soldiers protects the queen. She also has a trio of coroctopi (page 15) near her at all times. She has the support of most of her people, although this is based on fear.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 14 (Indie)

fields.name: Coroctopus

trait.name: Hold Breath
trait.text: While out of water, the coroctopus can hold its breath for 2 hours.

trait.name: Underwater Coral Camouflage
trait.text: The coroctopus has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made while underwater or anywhere near coral or rocks.

trait.name: Water Breathing
trait.text: The coroctopus can breathe only underwater.

action.name: Multiattack
action.text: The coroctopus makes two attacks with its tentacles.

action.name: Tentacle
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it is also grappled (escape DC 17). Until the grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the coroctopus can't use its tentacles on another target.

fields.description:
A school of brightly colored fish swims past a coral reef. Unexpectedly, part of the reef moves. Hiding there is a strange creature known as the coroctopus. It is an octopus that has formed out of coral. Strange energies came through a Riftgate and created this unusual monster.

	Rock Solid. The main reason this creature is so difficult to deal with is its hard body. The coroctopus' coral exterior provides ample protection against most attacks from predators.

	Coral Camouflage. The ability to hide underwater makes the coroctopus a deadly enemy. It is not uncommon for one of these monsters to seem to vanish underwater. They are quite skilled at camouflaging themselves.

	Fishermen's Friend. Local fishermen can actually benefit from the presence of this monster. It doesn't usually attack them and the coroctopus scares fish, crabs, and other creatures into the open.

Source:	Monsters of the Wilderness p. 15 (Indie)

fields.name: Coral Eel

trait.name: Illumination
trait.text: The coral eel sheds bright white light in a 20-foot radius.

trait.name: Water Breathing
trait.text: The coral eel can breathe only underwater.

action.name: Bite
action.text: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage. If a target is trapped in one of its bubbles, the coral eel makes its bite attack with advantage.

action.name: Bubble
action.text: The coral eel breathes out a magical bubble towards a Medium or smaller creature within 60 ft. The target must make a successful DC 15 Dexterity save or become restrained inside the bubble (escape DC 14). Inside the bubble, the target can breathe air. The bubble can be attacked (AC 8) from the outside. Any successful hit will destroy it and free the restrained creature.

fields.description:
These odd creatures can be seen from very far away. Coral eels are made from luminescent coral and radiate a bright white light. They seldom surprise their prey but they have a unique way of attacking.

	Deep Blue Sea. Coral eels enjoy colder waters but can be found in any ocean region. These creatures are constantly hunting for food sources. They also breathe out large magical bubbles to trap prey. This unusual attack takes many creatures by surprise.

	Bubble Trouble. These monstrosities are sometimes called bubble eels. Humanoids who live near their territory know to stay out of the water when they're around.
